text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Tuesday it planned to restructure it corporate centre in Eindhoven and that a reduction in the number of jobs there was unavoidable.
A Philips spokesman said over 800 people were employed at the centre, covering financial, legal, fiscal, press office and other administrative posts.
The spokesman said the move was independent of Monday's profit warning, which also referred to accelerating planned actions for recovery.

Philips on Monday said a previously forecast improvement in second half operating profit was unlikely based on preliminary information from the third quarter, causing its shares to close over two percent lower.

"This programme should ensure and enhance clear accountability at management level, eliminate excessive coordination, improve flexibility and reduce cost of organisation," a statement from Philips said.

The spokesman declined to say how many jobs might be lost at the centre and said that the last major round of job reductions at the headquarters had been during the opening phases of former chairman Jan Timmer's company-wide Centurion recovery programme in the early 1990s.
He would not comment on analysts' speculation that further steep job cuts to augment a 6,000 reduction announced in July were on the cards soon.
Analysts greeted yesterday's profits warning with predictions of their own that Philips might need to carry out restructuring, possibly involving job losses.

The spokesman said Cor Boonstra, who took over as chairman from Timmer on October 1, had recently referred to the need for a new management model aimed at cutting out over-elaboration in issuing orders and sending instructions around the world.

"Philips is going to have to eliminate a number of these activities. Employees must be given more opportunity to take responsibility themselves in their own organisational units," the Philips statement quoted Boonstra as saying recently. -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
